HOW IT'S MADEFour steps

01

Make the character sheets

One image per character: full body front, three quarter, profile and back, plus close-ups of the face and the props. You make it once and attach it to every video, so Mozart looks the same in every shot.

Mozart
Robot
02

Make one location per clip

Before any video, generate the place itself, seen from where the hidden camera will be. This is the step most people skip, and it is why their videos look random.

Music room
Jacuzzi salon
03

Generate the video

In Seedance 2.5, Reference mode, attach the location and the character sheet, paste the video prompt, 4:3. Test it at 480p first, then make the good one at 720p.

Location

04

Edit

Keep the best 2 to 3 seconds of each clip, hard cuts on the beat, one title card on the last shot and the music added inside Instagram.

WHY IT LOOKS REALThe hidden camera tricks

1

Someone is secretly filming

Every prompt says who is filming and from where: a servant behind a half open door. Something blurry in the foreground (a door, a column, a curtain) sells it instantly.

2

Clumsy zooms, late pans

"Zooms in two uneven steps, overshoots, pulls back a touch." Real people can't zoom smoothly. That imperfection is the realism.

3

The camera never freezes

AI video freezes the frame when people pose. Write "The camera never freezes" and describe the small shake, the breathing and the late reframing.

4

Nobody looks at the camera

The world doesn't know it's being filmed. The only look to camera is the payoff, and then it's a real reaction, not a pose.

5

Kill the AI look

Plain daylight, neutral colours, a little phone noise. Always add "no golden hour, no orange tint, no colour grading". That golden glow is what screams AI.
